groups.title: Crude speech
groups.q: Here the characters swear or speak crudely. Does each line sound natural?

rows.text: – May whoever denies Eagle Eye News be damned.
– Ugh, what do you want, Eskandar? What the hell is wrong with you?
– No name suits you, damn you.
– I'm telling you I can't see, asshole.
– If you don't give a fuck about the world or anything in it, why are you so obsessed with quizzes and exams?
– The answer is that kissing Master Hooman's ass doesn't suit you.
– What difference? If McCain gets in, he'll fuck Iran up, objectively.
– Ugh, what's with that shitty thinker pose again?
– Anyone who wants to spout philosophical bullshit can take it to the kitchen. The bulb's brighter in there too; it'll light up your brains.
– You useless prick ... hoooooh ... head down like that ... hooooh ... where are you going so fast?
– Pfff, damn you. You've become an expatriate now, so you don't give a damn about us. You foreigner-worshiping sellout.
– Shit-for-brains. You make me open my mouth and say it. I mean, did you only hear about it? Weren't you hit by it yourself?
– If age is what counts, then you should be licking Bahman's balls. He's at least five years older than us.
– Fuck this luck of ours.
– I would have preferred rooming with them instead of a dick-brain like you.
– So you're a fucking freshman.

– Murderous moves like this are just what I'd expect from you, but what I really want to know is what fucking maniac had his shop open at six on a Friday morning so you could go and buy a camera from him.
– If Kamyar hadn't been such a precious little shit and had stayed in the dorm, no bed would have opened up and landed us with these two marvels.
– So you mean our shitty luck in drawing an antique like you just keeps repeating?
– Again we reach that same damned discontinuity.
– I'm telling you, Eldie-jan, between us, you ended up abroad on a fucking fluke. If it weren't for Eagle Eye News, you'd still be here with us.
– What kind of shit is going on in that brain of yours now?
– You shat all over the mood that song had put me in with that fucking voice of yours.
– Fine, whatever the fuck.
– See what a fine mess you've made, you shit-for-brains.
– I'm looking for my glasses, asshole. Tell Farid to stop leaving his cup right in my way.

groups.title: Does it sound natural?
groups.q: Does each line sound natural and clear?

rows.text: – Then just think what our poor Baba must be going through: sitting idle at home all these years.
– Sure, Baba really hungers for respect. But he ended up with the wrong people; we've smashed every last bit of it.
– Whose cousin?
– Haven't you finished what you came for?
– I have no time at all this week. Next week, Thursday at three, the same place we met last time. I should also say I only have half an hour to spare.
– Aghhh. That made my skin crawl.
– Leopard Farid can't even make up his own mind. One minute he's pulling murderous moves; the next he's saying, "Oh, blood. That made my skin crawl."
– Where on my neck does it say foothold?
Never mind that. Why don't you pick up, no matter how many times I call? Did you divert my calls somewhere you shouldn't have?
– It's old age, neighbor.

– Objectively, just because we arrived a few days late, these Tehran kids, who only got into AmirKabir thanks to localization, act like we're the ones who came in through a quota, not them. Objectively.
– Man, don't talk to this one so politely; it'll go to his head. We took all those practice tests and ended up roommates with this antique.
– So you're all very clever boys.
At best, the dorm monitors got blue wall-to-wall carpeting instead of the dust-colored kind.
– It makes me so mad when you just sit there in silence like this. I want to punch you.
– No one's room has a carpet, Baba-jan. Only we have a carpet, and that's because we're the elite room.
– That's our question too.
– Fine, Eagle Eye, fine. Now don't stick your glasses into the laptop.
– If Fly were here, his antennae would prick up at once: What is this that pays off like that?
As soon as your name comes up, my ears prick up.
– Ah, if only one day I could pierce those ears of yours with my nails so they wouldn't prick up anymore.
– Now say whatever you want, but keep the final beit in mind.
– You're all like my own children.
– I've loved you for thirty-two months. From a distance. Without your knowing. In silence, without a single word.
– Amir, Grandpa caught Covid too, but you'd never know it; he shook it off like a simple cold. Probably because he can't hear and has no idea what's going on, and he never got scared.
